claims.text: High-resolution in situ aberration-corrected (S)TEM can investigate the thermal behavior of AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles at the atomic scale.
EDS/EELS compositional mapping during in situ heating can detect elemental redistribution or segregation in the nanoparticles.
The initial AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles are nearly equiatomic.
The initial AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles have a nominally homogeneous elemental distribution and a single-phase structure at ambient temperature.
Ex situ ambient-temperature characterization indicates no discernible elemental segregation or secondary phases in the initial nanoparticles.
Atomic-resolution TEM and compositional mapping can reveal heating-induced local atomic rearrangements or elemental segregation.
Configurational entropy in the five-element AuCoCuNiPt system thermodynamically suppresses large-scale phase separation under thermal stress.
Configurational entropy in the five-element system suppresses thermally induced morphological changes.
Nearly equiatomic AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles will remain compositionally and structurally uniform over a broad elevated-temperature range.
The nanoparticles will exhibit minimal coarsening up to approximately 600 °C.
The nanoparticles will exhibit minimal changes in size, shape, and composition over the selected temperature range.
At higher temperatures or longer annealing times, local diffusion may cause partial phase segregation or particle coalescence.
Kinetic and nanoscale interfacial effects may destabilize the nanoparticles despite the proposed configurational-entropy effect.
Detection of segregation, a new phase, or significant coarsening below 600 °C would falsify the stated thermal-stability hypothesis.
